questions.question: In a multi-tenant app, why does proxy.ts use NextResponse.rewrite rather than a redirect to map sharma-wealth.example.in/funds/42 to /sharma-wealth/funds/42?
options: Redirects are not allowed in proxy.ts
A rewrite serves the internal route while the browser keeps showing the tenant's own URL
A rewrite skips the [tenant] layout and is therefore faster
Rewrites automatically cache the tenant lookup
questions.explanation: The rewrite turns the Host header into a route segment internally; the visitor still sees their tenant's domain and path.

questions.question: Which practice best prevents Tenant A from seeing Tenant B's cached fund list?
options: Use a single shared tag such as "funds" for all revalidations
Resolve the tenant in proxy.ts with a database call on every request
Pass the tenant ID as an argument to every cached function so it becomes part of the cache key
questions.explanation: Cache keys must include the tenant. Tenant-scoped tags like funds:sharma-wealth also stop one tenant's update from purging everyone's cache.

questions.question: Why should links from the home zone to the blog zone use a plain a tag instead of Link?
options: Link prefetches and soft-navigates only within its own app, which does not work across zones
Link does not support absolute paths
Plain a tags enable Server Actions across zones
questions.explanation: Each zone is a separate Next.js app, so crossing zones is a hard navigation. Pages visited together should live in the same zone.

questions.question: What does setting assetPrefix: "/blog-static" in the blog zone achieve?
options: It makes the blog zone the default zone
It encrypts the blog zone's Server Actions
It serves the zone's JS and CSS under /blog-static/_next/... so they do not collide with other zones' assets
It moves all blog pages under the /blog-static path
questions.explanation: Every zone has its own /_next files; the prefix keeps them apart, and the default zone rewrites /blog-static/* to the blog zone.
